title: Asynchronous stall hunter — prototype log
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy notes from a small field-style experiment to surface and categorise asynchronous stalls in the inference path. Goal is to find reproducible triggers that cause 10–90ms mid-request stalls (not full coldstarts) under mixed-priority, continuous-batching workloads.

Context / motivation:
- Observed intermittent ~20–100ms micro-stalls in prod traces when we have simultaneous streaming and short-response qps.
- Hypothesis: stalls correlate with lock contention in the async I/O path (disk/mmap + RPC backpressure) combined with KV-cache misses that trigger small but blocking file reads or GC pressure during context swap.

Environment:
- 4x a2-large (8 vCPU, 1xA10G) local test nodes (simulated toy infra)
- Runtime: redwood-runtime-proto: v0.9.7-async-experiments
- Model: llama-ish-13B-quant8 (local snapshot)
- Harness: custom microdriver (nodejs) that can issue: streaming requests (chunked=true) + sync requests (single-shot) mixed at configurable ratios
- Seed data: short prompts median token length 18, 10% long prompts ~120 tokens

Test matrix (selected runs):
- A: baseline continuous-batch: qps=120, batch_timeout=8ms, batch_size_cap=64, stream:sync=0:1 (no streaming)
- B: mixed streaming: qps=120, same batch config, stream:sync=1:3 (25% streaming)
- C: streaming-heavy: qps=120, stream:sync=1:1
- D: smaller cap: qps=120, batch_size_cap=16, batch_timeout=2ms
- E: with simulated small disk read (mmap stutter): inject 50µs every 200ms on worker thread (file read path)

Measurement approach:
- Capture request-level timeline (events: recv, batch_assign, kernel_start, kernel_end, stream_chunk, response_complete)
- Instrument CPU and thread-blocking events (where possible) and Go runtime GC pauses for host process
- Collect p50/p90/p99 latency and micropause histogram (buckets: 1–5ms, 5–10ms, 10–25ms, 25–100ms)
- 60s warmup, then 10min run, single run each condition

Raw observations (representative figures):
- Run A (baseline): p50=34ms, p90=68ms, p99=118ms. Micropause buckets: 1–5ms:72%, 5–10ms:19%, 10–25ms:7%, 25–100ms:2%
- Run B (mixed streaming 25%): p50=36ms, p90=84ms, p99=165ms. Micropause: 1–5ms:64%, 5–10ms:18%, 10–25ms:10%, 25–100ms:8%
- Run C (1:1 streaming): p50=39ms, p90=96ms, p99=210ms. Micropause: 1–5ms:57%, 5–10ms:15%, 10–25ms:12%, 25–100ms:16%
- Run D (small cap): p50=41ms, p90=110ms, p99=245ms. Micropause shifted right (10–25ms:20%, 25–100ms:18%)
- Run E (+disk stutter): p50=46ms, p90=145ms, p99=380ms. Micropause: 1–5ms:40%, 5–10ms:12%, 10–25ms:18%, 25–100ms:30%

Quick per-run notes:
- A: stable baseline. Minimal micro-stalls; typical saturating batching pattern with continuous KV hits ~92%.
- B: introducing streaming increases p99 and tail mass; trace slices show batch_assign->kernel_start gap of ~20–80ms in ~6% of requests.
- C: further tailing; many of the large gaps coincide with a stream_chunk flush events that trigger a short flush syscall on the main thread.
- D: lowering batch cap increases frequency of small batches causing more kernel launches (more scheduling noise).
- E: deterministic small disk reads amplify the tail strongly. Correlations show the large stalls align with worker thread hitting the mmapRead path while another thread holds the I/O mutex (contention).

Trace excerpt (representative):
- Req 4721: recv 00:00:00.000 -> batch_assign 00:00:00.006 -> (wait) -> kernel_start 00:00:00.042 -> kernel_end 00:00:00.312 -> response_complete 00:00:00.315
  Observed: wait interval ~36ms between batch_assign and kernel_start. OS thread stack shows: syscall epoll_wait -> user-space channel send -> blocked on i/o-mmap-read mutex

Hypotheses from traces:
1) streaming flushes sometimes cause the event-loop thread to take a short syscall path that delays batch dispatch; this effect is amplified when I/O mutexes are contended by occasional mmap reads for KV-cache misses.
2) GC was visible on 2 runs but only contributed ~10ms spikes; majority stalls are I/O/lock related rather than full-stop GC.
3) Reducing batch cap increases scheduling overhead and increases tail, so unit economics tradeoff is real.

Small ASCII histogram (aggregate tail distribution p99 focus) — percent of requests with stall > threshold:
- >10ms: 18% (mixed runs), >25ms: 7%, >50ms: 3%, >100ms: 0.8%

Immediate mitigations tested quickly:
- Move small read path off main dispatch thread (spawn dedicated I/O worker + queue). Quick smoke: p99 dropped from 210ms -> 150ms in run C-ish re-run.
- Add micro-yield in streaming flush path (allow one iteration of event loop to process): minor improvement, p99 -6–8%.
- Increase batch_timeout slightly to 10ms to absorb jitter: reduces kernel churn but increases p50 by ~2–3ms. Tradeoff acceptable for tail improvement.

Actionable next steps:
- Build a small PoC where mmap/backing-file reads are routed through a dedicated threadpool (configurable). Test with injected stutter at higher freq to see mitigation robustness.
- Add fine-grained locking metrics around mmap cache (per-shard counters + contention timer). Put a lightweight Prometheus metric to surface "mmap_lock_hold_ms_total".
- Add an eBPF-based wakeup sampling to check syscalls that correlate with batch_assign delays (if ops is cool with sandbox).
- Parameter sweep: batch_timeout [2,4,8,12,20ms], batch_size_cap [16,32,64] with streaming ratios [0,0.25,0.5,0.75] — schedule overnight.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Could some of the stalls actually be kernel scheduling jitter under hypervisor? Need to repro with CPU affinity pinned vs unpinned.
- How does this scale with model size? Larger models have longer kernel_start->kernel_end which may amortize the stall impact. Might be less visible for 70B-ish.
- Re-check impact on throughput/cost if we force dedicated I/O threads per worker (resource vs tail benefit).

Quick appendix: commands used for harness
- driver: node harness.js --qps 120 --streamRatio 0.25 --batchTimeoutMs 8 --batchCap 64 --seed smallprompts.json
- trace collector: ./trace-collector -out trace-20250804-async.json -events recv,batch_assign,kernel_start,kernel_end,syscall
- injected stutter: ./stutter --target mmapRead --freq 200ms --dur 50us

Notes (log-ish):
- 2025-08-04 09:12 run A baseline: looks good
- 2025-08-04 09:36 run B: tail starts creeping
- 2025-08-05 14:04 verified overlay removing main-thread mmap returns p99 improvements
- 2025-08-07 11:21 collab sync w/ Ravi — agree to prototype dedicated IO pool

TODOs:
- [ ] PoC: io-threadpool routing (Daphne)
- [ ] Add mmap lock metrics (Ravi)
- [ ] Schedule parameter sweep + record (Leah)
- [ ] Small write-up for infra-threading tradeoffs for eng-sync retro

Quirks observed (for writeup):
- Reproducing on GCP preemptible instances behaves differently — less tail in some runs; may be due to kernel scheduler differences.
- Windows Subsystem yields very different syscall latencies; not relevant but worth noting for local devers.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy into a proper experiment doc if PoC shows promising regression in tail.
